fields.description:
## Context / Problem
When a compaction sweep holds the store write lock, a blocked session cannot tell what is
holding it or whether interrupting it is safe. Both facts are already known to the code and
neither reaches the operator.

From a live incident on 2026-08-13, reported by a session in a different lane
(`vigilant-erasable-pony`): a sweep held `.tickets-tracker/.ticket-write.lock` for 24+ minutes
at 0.0% CPU. What that session saw was:

    flock: could not acquire lock after 181s (holder: host=... pid=... held=47s)

A bare pid. Identifying it as compaction required `lsof` and `ps`. A second sweep, spawned by a
different worktree's close, blocked the same session again minutes later — the blast radius is
host-wide across worktrees, so "check your own checkout" does not help either.

The information gap is the whole problem, because the answer is already documented:
`compact_trigger.run_sweep` guarantees "a skipped sweep is a no-op for correctness (the events
stay live and the next trigger folds them)". An operator holding that guarantee can safely
SIGTERM the holder. An operator looking at an unattributed pid cannot distinguish it from a
mystery hang mid-write, and the safe response to that is to wait — which is exactly wrong here.
One sweep was ultimately killed manually (pid 98440, 26 minutes) to unblock three agents.

## Approach
Say what the holder is, and say that it is interruptible — at the two places a blocked writer
already looks.

**1. Label the lock holder, ambiently.** `lock_owner._owner_stamp` writes the v2 ownership
line (`rebar-lock v2 host=... ns=... pid=... start=...`) that `describe_lock_holder` renders
into every `LockTimeout`. That stamp is written by `_acquire_mkdir` (`lock.py`), reached only
through `lock.acquire`. Add an optional operation label to that stamp so the timeout reads
`... pid=98440 held=181s op=compact-sweep` instead of a bare pid.

The label must reach `_owner_stamp` WITHOUT editing the acquisition call site, because the
sweep's store-write-lock acquisition is `lock.acquire()` in `compact_txn._compact_locked`
(`compact_txn.py:358`), invoked per ticket, and `compact_txn.py` is deliberately NOT in this
ticket's scope (it carries the freshly-landed sweep-perf change `mesodermic-vaporish-seaslug`
and must not be re-touched here). The mechanism that satisfies this is an AMBIENT label, not a
new parameter threaded through `acquire`:

- `lock_owner.py` gains a process/thread-local operation label — a `contextvars.ContextVar`
  plus a `operation_label(label)` context manager that sets it on enter and resets it on exit.
  `_owner_stamp()` reads that contextvar and, when set, appends a single colon-free `op=<label>`
  field to the stamp it already builds. When unset (every ordinary writer) the stamp is
  byte-identical to today's.
- The sweep sets that contextvar around its whole body at its two entry points
  (`compact_trigger.run_sweep` and `compact.py`'s sweep loop). Every `lock.acquire` that runs
  beneath that `with` block — including the per-ticket `lock.acquire()` inside
  `compact_txn._compact_locked`, which this ticket does not modify — therefore writes its owner
  stamp with `op=compact-sweep`. The data flow is sweep-entry → contextvar → `_owner_stamp`, so
  the label reaches the stamp ambiently and `compact_txn.py` needs no change. `contextvars` is
  the correct carrier here because the label is read synchronously in the SAME process/thread
  that later calls `acquire`; the sweep runs its folds inline (`_sweep_one_ticket` →
  `compact_cli` → `_compact_locked`), so the ambient value is in scope at the acquisition.

The v2 format has a documented forward-compatibility contract that must be preserved exactly:
the line is deliberately COLON-FREE so an older rebar parsing it with the legacy
`host, sep, pid = stamp.partition(":")` finds no separator and declines to act
(`_store/lock.py` module docstring, bug castoff-tigerseye-ammonite). A new `key=value` field
keeps that property (the label value is sanitized to strip any `:`, `=`, or whitespace so it
stays a single colon-free token), and `_parse_v2_stamp` already tolerates unknown fields, so an
older reader ignores it rather than misparsing. The label is descriptive only — it must never
influence reclamation, exactly as the existing fields do not: `_stamp_is_stale` /
`stamped_file_is_stale` never read `op=`.

**2. State the remedy in the error.** When the holder is labelled as optional housekeeping,
`LockTimeout`'s message should say so and name the safe action, rather than leaving the reader
to find a docstring in `compact_trigger`. `describe_lock_holder` renders the `op=` field into
the holder string, and `LockTimeout` recognises the known interruptible label (`compact-sweep`)
in that holder string and appends a remedy line: that the holder is a compaction sweep, that
interrupting it loses no data, and that the next trigger re-folds. An ordinary (unlabelled)
holder gets no remedy line.

Deliberately NOT proposed here: auto-killing a long-running sweep. That is a policy decision
about pre-empting one process from another, it needs its own justification, and the reported
incidents were all resolved by a human with the right information. Give the human the
information first.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_store/lock_owner.py` — an ambient operation-label contextvar + `operation_label`
  context manager; `_owner_stamp` appends an optional colon-free `op=` field (sanitized to a
  single token) when the contextvar is set; a small helper mapping a known interruptible label
  to its remedy text. The label is ignored by older readers and NEVER consulted by staleness
  logic.
- `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` — render the `op=` label in `describe_lock_holder`; extend the
  `LockTimeout` message with the safe-to-interrupt remedy when the holder string names a known
  interruptible operation.
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py` — wrap `run_sweep`'s body in
  `lock_owner.operation_label("compact-sweep")` so the store-lock acquisitions it drives
  (transitively, via `compact_all_cli` → `_compact_locked`) stamp the label. This is the
  ambient carrier described above, not an edit to any acquisition call.
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact.py` — wrap the sweep loop (`compact_all_cli`/`_run_sweep`) in
  the same `operation_label("compact-sweep")`, so a direct `rebar compact-all` invocation (not
  only the trigger) is labelled end to end.
- `tests/unit/test_lock_holder_labelling.py` — new tests.

Note on portability: the mechanism is a colon-free `key=value` field written to the lock stamp
file and a `contextvars` label set in-process — no CI provider, no external service, no
platform-specific facility is involved, so it works identically on any environment that can run
rebar (with or without CI).

## Testing
- A labelled holder appears in `describe_lock_holder` output and in the `LockTimeout` message
  (asserting the message contains `op=compact-sweep`, not only a pid).
- The remedy text (safe / lossless / next-trigger-refolds) is PRESENT in the `LockTimeout`
  message for a labelled optional holder and ABSENT for an ordinary writer.
- An UNLABELLED holder renders exactly as today (byte-identical `describe_lock_holder` output),
  so ordinary writers see no format change.
- The stamp stays colon-free with the label present, so the documented legacy-reader refusal
  still holds; and a label containing `:`/`=`/whitespace is sanitized to a single token.
- `_parse_v2_stamp` accepts a stamp carrying an unknown extra field, proving forward
  compatibility in the other direction.
- Reclamation is unaffected: a labelled stale lock and an unlabelled stale lock are treated
  identically by `stamped_file_is_stale` / `_stamp_is_stale`.
- End to end: with `operation_label("compact-sweep")` active, a real `lock.acquire` writes an
  owner stamp carrying the label — i.e. the ambient contextvar reaches `_owner_stamp` through
  the actual acquisition path, the same path `compact_txn._compact_locked` uses — and a
  subsequent `describe_lock_holder` / `LockTimeout` names it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A blocked writer's `LockTimeout` names the holder as a compaction sweep — a test asserts
      the message contains the operation label rather than only a pid.
- [ ] That message states the interruption is safe and lossless — a test asserts the remedy
      text is present for a labelled optional holder and ABSENT for an ordinary writer.
- [ ] An unlabelled holder's rendering is byte-identical to today's — a test pins the existing
      format so ordinary writers see no change.
- [ ] The stamp remains colon-free with a label, and `_parse_v2_stamp` ignores unknown fields —
      tests assert both directions of the forward-compat contract.
- [ ] Staleness and reclamation decisions ignore the label entirely — a test asserts a labelled
      and an unlabelled stale lock are adjudicated identically.
- [ ] The label reaches the stamp through the real acquisition path via the ambient contextvar
      (proving the sweep-entry → contextvar → `_owner_stamp` flow works without editing
      `compact_txn.py`) — a test drives `lock.acquire` under `operation_label(...)` and asserts
      the written stamp carries `op=compact-sweep`.
- [ ] The full local gate set plus CI's pytest tiers pass.
